newsitem.title: USA: Enamelon to launch toothpaste in six weeks.
newsitem.headline: Enamelon to launch toothpaste in six weeks.

text.p: Enamelon Inc on Friday said test marketing would begin within six weeks on a new toothpaste designed to prevent cavities.
A national rollout of the product is scheduled to begin in first quarter of 1998.
Shares of Yonkers-based Enamelon was 1-1/2 higher at 14-1/8 in early afternoon trading.

Enamelon said its toothpaste stregthened tooth enamel from the inside out by adding calcium, phosphate and fluride ions to teeth during brushing. The ions enter the teeth and create a stronger molecular structure.

Enamelon's product is the only fluoride toothpaste clinically proven to be better at "hardening and remineralizing teeth than the leading fluoride toothpaste," Rodman & Renshaw analyst Anthony Viscogliosi said in a research alert.

Yonkers, N.Y.-based Enamelon will present its clinical research data at a dental conference in March. The findings are from animal and in vitro laboratory studies. Enamelon is in the process of conducting about 20 human clinical studies.

"Publications in scientific and professional journals will be integral in gaining acceptance and support with the dentists and oral hygienists. Support of the dental community will play a crucial role in promoting the product to consumers," Viscogliosi said.
Rodman & Renshaw on Friday reiterated a buy rating on the stock and set a price target of $13 a share. He did not specify a time frame for the target price.
Enamelon Chairman Steven Fox said the new toothpaste was "the most important advance in dental care since the introduction of fluoride."
Fox said he expected Enamelon would seize a "sizable share" of the $1.8 billion U.S oral-care products market. He declined to be more specific.
Rodman & Renshaw expected Enamelon, which launched its initial public offering in October, to post $28.2 million in revenues in 1998.

While Enamelon holds the exclusive licenses from the American Dental Assocation Health Foundation to use the new technology, it will face a battle against leading products such as Procter & Gamble Co's Crest and Colgate-Palmolive Co's Colgate, analysts said.
"Clearly, Crest and Colgate are not going to lie down," said Edward Tenthoff, a Rodman & Renshaw analyst.
Crest and Colgate hold about 47 percent of the toothpaste market combined though their grip has slipped since the new toothpastes, such as baking soda products, began attracting fans, Tenthoff said.
With Enamelon entering the market, "the majors will beef up their commercials with more clinical claims for fluoride," he said.
Analysts expect Enamelon to launch a secondary equity offering to help fund a national advertising campaign next year.

As Enamelon's new product gains attention, the company is expected to become an attractive acquisition target. Enamelon's six patents and 12 pending patents would represent valuable assets for the more established toothpaste marketers, analysts said.
